After discussing this on Discord, abandon this review in favor of a set of smaller more manageable reviews which I'll create in the coming days.

If it's an ASRR system, I think meta-asrock might be a more appropriate place for it to live than meta-ampere?  (Setting aside potential confusion about ASRock vs ASRock Rack, which...if they can hardly make up their minds about what's what, I dunno how much we should worry about it.)  By analogy, lots of x86 server platforms that OpenBMC supports use Intel CPUs, but meta-intel-openbmc only has the s2600wf platform (an Intel-made board).

I chose meta-ampere because it's using more Ampere-specific than ASRock-specific functionality. For example I want to support the Ampere IPMI OEM commands and monitor boot status via the SMPro (meta-ampere/meta-common/recipes-ampere/host/ac01-boot-progress). Would it be allowed to pick recipes from meta-ampere/meta-common if this lives in meta-asrock?

If there's infrastructure that's specific to Ampere-CPU-based platforms but not Ampere *boards*, maybe that stuff should get "promoted" out of `meta-ampere` to a common area, e.g. something roughly analogous to `meta-phosphor/recipes-x86`?

I talked to the person leading the OpenBMC team at Ampere and he wants me to put the code in meta-asrock. So I've updated the changeset to put it under meta-asrock/meta-altrad8, and will try and make some more fixes based on review comments before pushing it here.
The latest revision moves it to meta-asrock/meta-altrad8, with recipes common to Ampere Altra systems in meta-asrock/meta-ampere.

Glad to see that another ASRock Rack platform is being upstreamed! While this is still WIP, please note that Patch files aren't allowed in upstream, and issues that these patch files solve should be rather addressed in the relevant upstream repositories (if it is really required).

On a side note, the ALTRAD8UD platform has an interesting issue (maybe a design bug) that causes the SPI address width to change on a watchdog timeout, causing the BMC not to boot anymore.
Please fix the whitespace issues shown in pink throughout this review.

after looking at the kernel source it appears the label is deprecated but takes priority when creating the userspace name.

I read the documentation that the label is deprecated, but phosphor-led-sysfs wasn't happy until I added it.

SysfsLed::getLedDescr says the node can be any of
```
 * - devicename:color:function
 * - devicename::function
 * - color:function (e.g. "red:fault")
 * - label (e.g. "identify")
 * - :function (e.g. ":boot")
 * - color: (e.g. "green:")
```

But then the code has:
```
    if (words.size() != 3)
    {
        lg2::warning(
            "LED description '{DESC}' not well formed, expected 3 parts but got {NPARTS}",
            "DESC", name, "NPARTS", words.size());
    }
```

my point is that the generic code should be able to synsthise a name from the other components.   maybe you should concentrate on what the description should be?   I'm assuming it's looking at the name and not looking up the label in the device tree.

If I remove the label property, it gets a name of e.g. 'green:indicator' instead of 'platform:green:indicator'. Unfortunately that won't work with phosphor-leds-sysfs which requires the name to have 3 parts. Also, other dts files use the label property.

IMO, copying `x86-power-control` into the main tree and modifying it to the needs of the platform is not a useful solution. Keeping the code in sync with upstream will become unnecessarily complex (and as Milton has pointed out, it has no CI coverage this way).

I see two options here:
- Use `phosphor-state-manager` and write the power control in multiple scripts (similar to what has been done in `yosemite4`)
- Open a discussion if the power control daemon really have to be limited x86 platforms only, or if it could be opened for non-x86 platforms too (i.e. making POST Complete assertion optional and such).
I think moving to PSM is the right thing to do. I've implemented the scripts.
